brief: A bright, daylit Scandinavian-style cafe with a full-height glazed street frontage and a timber-framed door. Along the glass runs a window bar of tall oak stools, with potted fiddle-leaf and olive trees filling the corners. The middle of the room is open pale oak plank floor with round marble bistro tables and square light-oak tables, each seated with woven-rush oak chairs. The long white vertical-slat counter runs along the right and back, topped with white marble, with an espresso machine and two grinders, cake domes, a flower vase and a glass pastry case. Behind it, open oak shelves hold cups, jars, coffee bags and trailing plants under a large framed blackboard menu. White pendants and white track spots give soft support light, but sun dappling through the street trees is the main light. Tables carry cappuccinos, croissants, small flower vases and notebooks.

must_have.where: on the counter, espresso machine with two grinders
large framed blackboard centred on the back wall
round marble and square light-oak tables in the middle of the room
long tall oak ledge table along the street glazing
oak stools at the window bar
olive tree and fiddle-leaf figs by the windows and counter

concept: A Scandinavian daylit bakery-cafe where pale oak, white slat panelling and white marble are warmed by street-tree sunlight, greenery and woven-rush seating.
relations: Pale oak floor + light oak furniture + white painted slat counter and walls = a bright, airy, low-contrast palette that bounces the daylight
Full-height glazing + sparse white pendants + 3000K warm bulbs = daylight is the key light and fixtures only add a gentle warm accent
Woven-rush seats + marble tabletops + plants and flowers = soft natural texture against a clean white background
Open oak shelves + blackboard menu + pastry case concentrate the visual interest on the counter wall, leaving the floor open
Moderate seating density with a window bar keeps the room relaxed and lets people look out at the street
not_reproducible: Street trees, cars and buildings outside, dappled sun patterns, real food and pastries, coffee cups, people, books and notebooks, bottles and coffee bags, the espresso machine's fine detail.
